newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch firm buying Providian's insurance business.
newsitem.headline: Dutch firm buying Providian's insurance business.

text.p: Dutch insurer Aegon NV said Monday it was buying the insurance business of Providian Corp. of Louisville for $2.62 billion in stock -- the biggest acquisition in the U.S. life insurance industry.
The deal is the latest in a rapidly consolidating global industry pressured by high costs and tough competition from banks and mutual funds all chasing consumer savings.

"Consolidation in the insurance sector will certainly continue in Europe and the United States. Market shares are diminishing and European union will accelerate this process," said Dutch-based IRIS analyst Bart van der Feen.

Aegon said the deal, which will make it one of the top three European insurance companies and 11th biggest in the United States, would be a tax-free stock transaction providing Providian shareholders $28 for each share they own, which would be worth about $2.62 billion.
Aegon also said its U.S. unit would assume debt worth $780 million and preferred stock worth $100 million as part of the deal, which is expected to close in the middle of next year.
Providian stockholders will also receive shares in Providian Bancorp, which will be spun off as an independent banking company.
"We weren't interested in the banking side. We want to stay with our core (insurance) business," Aegon Chairman Kees Storm told reporters.
Aegon said the acquisition would increase its earnings by about 5 percent in 1998.
Providian, which employs 8,600 staff, is active throughout the United States, operating in four divisions -- Providian Bancorp, Direct Insurance Group, Agency Group and Capital Management Group.
Hague-based Aegon, with a global workforce of almost 20,000, operates in the Netherlands, the United States, Britain, Spain and Hungary.

"This record-setting acquisition is fully in line with Aegon's stated strategy. It is earnings enhancing, highly compatible and will provide a healthy boost to our growth into the next century," Storm said.
He added that the U.S. division's profit margin should increase because of the deal.
Analysts welcomed the deal, particularly the swift positive effect on earnings per share.
"This is a very positive acquisition. Looking at the EPS (earnings per share), we expect an increase of between four and eight percent," said Van der Feen, who maintained a buy rating on Aegon stock.
"One of the main points is that the deal is to be mainly financed internally without a major share issue," he added.
Aegon shares jumped on the news, adding 8 guilders ($4.59), or more than 8 percent, to 107.2 guilders ($61.47) on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange.
Providian's stock closed Friday at $52.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
